_doc: TEMPLATE — copy this to config/hosts/<your-host-id>.json and edit. This is the whole contract for adding a machine to the console: there is no code to write. The filename IS the host id and must equal the `id` field below (scripts/host-profiles.test.mjs enforces it). After copying, register the profile in the HOST_PROFILES map and the `known` set in next.config.ts — two one-line edits, listed at the bottom of this file. Every `_doc` and `note` key is stripped at load time and exists only for whoever reads this next. This template is validated by the same test suite as the real profiles, so it cannot silently rot.
name: Example Box
_doc_selection: HOW THIS PROFILE GETS CHOSEN: HOST_ID env var → a hostname equal to this id (case-insensitive, .local stripped) → platform inference → the default profile. So naming the file after the machine's actual hostname is usually all the wiring needed. Resolution happens ONCE, in next.config.ts, and is published as NEXT_PUBLIC_HOST_ID; see src/lib/host.ts.
_doc_platform: win32 | darwin | linux. Drives platform-specific probes — notably how the GPU is read (nvidia-smi vs. IOAccelerator counters).
_doc_gpu: nvidia | apple | none. `none` is legitimate: a CPU-only box still runs the console, still supervises services, and simply reports no accelerator.

memory._doc: THE MOST IMPORTANT FIELD IN THE FILE. `kind` decides whether VRAM and system RAM are one budget or two, and that reshapes the UI and the model-fit maths. discrete → a card and a host with SEPARATE budgets; give vramTotalGb and ramTotalGb, and the console shows two bars and refuses a model that will not fit the card. unified → Apple silicon, ONE pool shared by CPU and GPU; give totalGb only, and the console shows a single Memory bar and treats a model's footprint as one number. Getting this wrong does not error — it silently budgets against the wrong ceiling. Totals are a last-resort label used only until live telemetry arrives.

_doc_logsDir: Where per-service uvicorn access logs live, for the Requests tab's traffic tail. `~` is expanded. null means this host keeps no such directory — the tab still works, it just has no on-disk history to read.
_doc_commandsFile: scripts/<file> that scripts/manager.cjs reads start commands from. Each host gets its own, because the command that starts vLLM on a Windows box is not the command that starts it anywhere else. Create it alongside this profile; without it the manager has nothing to Start.
_doc_services: Everything this machine runs. `id` is referenced by workstreams, footprints and the tab-availability maps, so treat it as stable. Ports must be unique. A service listed here appears on the Services page whether or not it is running — that is the point: a host says what it HAS, and the console reports which of those are up.

services.name: Service Manager
services.note: scripts/manager.cjs — the supervisor every Start/Stop button goes through. Every host needs one. When it is down the console reports 'Manager error: fetch failed' on every service and nothing can be started, which is why it is a visible card rather than invisible infrastructure.

services.name: vLLM (Your Model)
services.note: An OpenAI-compatible chat service. metricsPath is optional and names a path serving Prometheus-format counters (vLLM does; Ollama does not). Declaring it is what lets the console show live telemetry without any route naming a service - a host that publishes none simply reports none instead of erroring. `serves.text` is what makes the box routable for text WITHOUT anything naming this service in code; `llm.model` additionally marks it selectable in the LLM picker. Where both are present they MUST agree — the test suite fails the build otherwise. Both carry the served-model-name to send as `model` in /v1/chat/completions, which is frequently NOT the same string as the model's Hub id.

services.name: Whisper STT
services.note: Capability ids are exactly: text, vision, image, stt, tts. A typo here does not error — the matching tab quietly reports itself unavailable on a box that works fine. The Speech tab resolves on the stt/tts CAPABILITY, never on a service being named 'whisper', so you can put any ASR model behind this and the tab keeps working.

services.name: Grafana
services.note: category: ai | monitoring | app. The distinction is how you USE it, not whether it touches the GPU: `app` is something you open and drive by hand in a browser (its card CTA becomes 'Open ↗'), `ai` is a headless model server other code calls. ComfyUI is categorised `app` for exactly this reason despite being the heaviest GPU consumer on its box.

services.name: AI Router
services.note: localOnly: this NEVER leaves the box. getServiceUrl() returns localUrl for it even from a deployed build, so a hosted console physically cannot route to it. Set this on anything that is a bare HTTP API with no auth of its own — such a thing must never acquire a public hostname, and marking it here is stronger than remembering not to give it one.

_doc_publicUrl: publicUrl is only ever used when the console runs somewhere OTHER than this machine (VERCEL is set); locally, getServiceUrl() always returns localUrl. Write the domain as ${PUBLIC_DOMAIN} rather than a literal hostname — it is substituted at load time from the PUBLIC_DOMAIN env var and falls back to example.com. This keeps the list of what a machine exposes out of the repository. If a host has no off-box address at all, set publicUrl equal to localUrl, as `manager` does above.
_doc_authRequired: true means the public hostname sits behind Cloudflare Access, so a DEPLOYED console must present CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID / CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET (see .env.example). It has no effect locally. Setting it true without providing the token does not fail loudly — the service reports UP and returns an HTML login page to every call.
_doc_workstreams: What this machine can be asked to DO, as the Home page offers it. Keys are fixed: text | image | audio | files. DECLARE ONLY WHAT THIS HOST CAN ACTUALLY BACK — this section exists because the Home page used to hardcode one machine's four workstreams, so every other host advertised work it could not do and offered buttons into tabs that were not there. `serviceId` must name a service in the array above. vramGb/ramGb are measured footprints, used by the pre-flight 'can it run?' panel. `color` is one of orange | violet | blue | emerald; the icon is chosen in code.
_doc_finally: TWO EDITS OUTSIDE THIS FILE, then you are done: (1) src/lib/host.ts — import the JSON and add it to HOST_PROFILES; (2) next.config.ts — add the id to the `known` set in detectHostId(). The duplication is deliberate and commented there: next.config.ts cannot import from src/, and host.ts must not import `os` because two client components pull in the service registry. Then run `npm test` — host-profiles.test.mjs validates every file in this directory, including this one.
